generalizedRange: Thar Desert of western Rajasthan, with a remnant in Kutch, Gujarat
hook: Near fifteen kilos and it still flies. Seventy now hatched by hand.

story.text: Just over a metre tall and close to fifteen kilograms, the Great Indian Bustard is among the heaviest birds that still fly.
Its booming call has been likened to thunder; at yearly leks males inflate and leap at one another.
A female lays one egg on open ground and carries her chick from danger under her wing.
Hunting and egg collection left about 1,260 birds by 1969; by 2018 some 150 remained, nearly all in India.
Heavy and low-flying, it never evolved to avoid wires: about 18 a year died on Thar power lines in 2017–18 — a fifth of the species.
India's Supreme Court took up the wires in 2021 and in December 2025 fixed a Rajasthan priority area: critical lines underground, no new turbines.
Since 2019 the Wildlife Institute of India has hatched wild-laid eggs at Sam, near Jaisalmer; the first captive-bred chick arrived in March 2023.
By March 2026 the Jaisalmer centres held seventy birds, up from sixteen in 2022, with first soft releases due this year.
That month an egg rode nineteen hours by road to Kutch, where a wild female hatched Gujarat's first chick in a decade.
To witness the Great Indian Bustard is to stand with the Bishnoi villagers who lent their grassland to it — and with the open horizon it needs.

stats.size: Just over 1 m tall · males near 15 kg

reproduction.text: She lays a single egg on bare ground and may lay again up to five times in a season, yet in the wild only about a quarter of eggs hatch — and the chick that does is carried from danger under her wing.

insight.text: In 2017–18 the power lines in about 4,000 square kilometres of the Thar were estimated to kill some 90,000 birds of 49 species a year — and roughly 18 of them were Great Indian Bustards, from a species of perhaps 150.

programs.title: Bustard Recovery Program
programs.summary: Hatches wild-laid eggs at the Sam and Ramdevra centres near Jaisalmer, tracks tagged birds, maps the power lines that need burying, and trains forest staff across the bustard states.

programs.title: Khetolai grassland reserve
programs.summary: Fenced 35 hectares of Bishnoi community grassland at Khetolai against free-ranging dogs and wild boar, cleared invasive Prosopis, and runs camera-trap surveys with local community officers.
